title: 智能写在一种我们还不懂的语言里
excerpt: 大模型也许并非没有抽象能力。它可能正在使用一种与人类数学 ontology 不同的语言压缩世界。真正的 interpretability，或许应该先发现这种机器原生语言，再研究如何把它翻译给人。
html:
模型内部也许并不混乱。真正的问题可能是，那里的规律写在一种我们还没有学会的语言里。

最近我越来越觉得，我们谈论“智能”时，常常把几个不同的问题混在了一起：知识、能力、抽象、可计算性与可理解性。

今天的大模型很容易制造一种直觉。只要参数、数据和推理时间继续增加，最终似乎就会出现一个统一的超级智能，把所有任务都做好。这个想象暗含了一个并不显然的等式：既然知识可以被统一进一个模型，能力也应该能够被统一。

我怀疑这个等式并不成立。知识可以共享一个广泛底座，但能力取决于系统用什么 primitive 切分问题，用什么坐标组织搜索，又用什么接口把结果变成可验证的行动。更进一步，模型也许已经拥有 abstraction，只是这些 abstraction 没有按照人类熟悉的 ontology 排列。

这不是“模型内部一定藏着一套外星科学”的宣言。它是一个可以被比较、被证伪的研究假设。

能力依赖表示，但“表示”不是一个分数

人类记录下来的知识确实很适合被一个大模型进行广泛而有损的统计压缩。书籍、论文、网页、代码与对话虽然结构不同，最终都能转化为训练信号。Foundation model 的意义正在于训练于广泛数据，并能被适配到许多下游任务。Bommasani et al., 2021

但 capability 不只是“参数里有没有相关信息”。它还取决于任务在当前系统中是否容易被表达、发现、执行和验证。

Python、SQL、Lean 与汇编语言都能描述复杂计算，却提供了完全不同的 primitive。SQL 让 relation、selection 与 join 成为短表达，Lean 让 proposition、type 与 proof obligation 成为可操作对象。Matthias Felleisen 对 programming language expressiveness 的经典分析指出，两种语言即使原则上能计算同样的函数，也不意味着一种语言的构造能在另一种语言里被局部而自然地表达。Felleisen, 1991

因此，与其把 capability 写成一个看似精确的总分，不如把它看成一个成本轮廓：

C_R(f) := (L_R(f), S_R(f), E_R(f), V_R(f))

其中，L 是描述任务与解法所需的长度，S 是搜索成本，E 是执行成本，V 是验证成本。它们单位不同，也未必能直接相加。一种表示可能让答案更短，却让验证更难；另一种表示可能执行更慢，却更适合证明。真正有意义的是比较这些维度上的支配关系与 Pareto trade-off。

这也解释了为什么“都是 universal computer”是一个过于宽松的共同点。可计算性只回答原则上能不能实现，不回答需要多少资源，也不回答一个规律是否容易被发现。Turing 的不可判定性结果进一步说明，universal computation 并不带来 universal prediction。Turing, 1936

所以必须保留几条分界：

computable ≠ efficiently computable

>

compressible ≠ discoverable

>

represented ≠ understandable

智能的差别也许很大一部分存在于一种“计算的几何”中：哪些计算在某种表示下变得短、自然、可发现、可验证并且可复用。

最强的反论证：LLM 本来就在学习人类 ontology

如果 LLM 的训练数据主要是人类文本，那么“它形成了完全异质的 ontology”并不是默认结论。文本本身已经是人类概念、分类与因果叙述的产物，训练目标又要求模型继续生成可被人类理解的 token。相比 AlphaZero 这类主要通过 self-play 学习的系统，语言模型受到的人类语义约束显然更强。

因此，这篇文章需要一个更窄也更可信的主张：

LLM 的输入输出 ontology 很大程度上来自人类，但实现这些语义行为的内部 computational factorization 不一定复制人类的概念边界。

编译器能接受人类写下的程序，也能输出符合人类 specification 的结果，却可能在中间表示里合并、拆分或重排我们的高层对象。类似地，一个模型可以流利地使用“因果”“讽刺”或“欺骗”等词，而不必在内部为每个词保留一个边界清楚的对应物。

异质 ontology 的先验会在一些条件下变强：训练信号主要来自图像、传感器或科学仪器，而不是语言；系统通过 self-play 或长期 reinforcement learning 自己发现策略；它拥有与人类不同的 body、memory 与 time scale；或者多个 AI 为了效率发展出人类不参与的通信协议。也就是说，这个假设对所有 AI 并不应当同样强。

三个竞争假设，以及什么能让它们失败

“我们暂时看不懂模型内部”至少兼容三种不同解释。把它们分开，才能让讨论离开黑箱隐喻。

H1：模型形成了异质但稳定的 abstraction。 如果成立，我们应该能找到跨输入、训练 seed 或邻近模型仍然稳定的 machine-native relation。它们在压缩、迁移或因果干预上会优于人类预设的 basis，同时又不容易被少数现成标签穷尽。某些结构还可能被转化为人类可以学习的 bridge concept。

H2：模型根本没有可复用的稳定 abstraction。 在这种情况下，我们会看到脆弱、分散而强烈依赖上下文的机制。干预效果难以局部化，候选 feature 无法跨任务迁移，不同训练运行之间也找不到稳定关系。所谓“机器语言”只是一种浪漫化投射。

H3：模型使用的仍是近似人类式 abstraction，只是我们尚未解码。 如果更好的 nonlinear decoder、representation alignment 或 causal test 最终能恢复一组接近人类概念、而且对行为具有充分解释力的变量，那么没有必要诉诸异质 ontology。

这三种假设要求不同的证据。发现一个可以被命名的 neuron 不能自动证明 H3，发现一个难以命名的 feature 也不能自动证明 H1。关键在于比较哪一种表示更稳定、更能压缩行为、更能跨情境迁移，并在干预后给出更准确的预测。

表示不只描述答案，它还塑造搜索

同一条周期规律，用一串逐时刻采样值表示时，修改频率可能需要同时改动许多数字；用 amplitude、frequency 与 phase 表示时，它只需要改变一个变量。两个坐标系描述同一个信号，却为学习制造了不同的 neighborhood。

搜索成本因此不仅取决于任务与表示，也取决于搜索算法与预算：

S_R(f; A, B)

一个 abstraction 的力量，不只是把已经找到的答案写短，而是把原本相距很远的候选解放进同一个局部邻域，让有限的 agent 可以用几步变化到达它们。Information geometry 提供了一个具体例子。普通 gradient descent 的“最陡方向”依赖参数坐标，natural gradient 则使用 Fisher geometry，让更新更接近模型分布本身的局部结构。Amari, 1998

神经网络里的 superposition 又解释了为什么人类概念未必会整齐地对齐单个 neuron。当潜在 feature 很稀疏，而可用维度有限时，模型可以把多个 feature 叠加在共享方向中。Elhage et al., 2022 于是，一个 neuron 的 polysemanticity 可能部分来自坐标选择，而不代表内部没有结构。

但这项结果只提供了一种 coordinate complexity 的机制，不能单独证明完整的 machine ontology。我们仍然需要区分：notation 只是符号不同；representation 改变坐标、分解与邻近关系；ontology 则连什么算对象、关系、原因与可干预变量都改变了。

中文母语者学习英文可以提供一个有限的类比。流利并不是把“狗”替换为 dog，再逐词搬运句子，而是重新决定哪些信息必须显式表达、谁成为 grammatical subject、一个场景怎样才会在目标语言里显得自然。Translation 不是 substitution，而是 representation change。不过中文和英文仍共享人的身体与世界，所以它们之间的距离通常小于人类与真正 machine-native ontology 之间可能存在的距离。

AlphaZero 同时展示了收敛与新概念

现有证据并不只支持“机器与人不同”。McGrath 等人研究 self-play 训练的 AlphaZero，发现许多人类棋类概念可以从其网络中被线性解码，而且这些概念会随着训练逐渐出现。McGrath et al., 2022 这是一个重要的收敛证据：即使没有人类棋谱监督，共享的任务结构也可能推动机器重新发现人类认识到的对象。

但收敛不是全部。Schut 等人进一步从 AlphaZero 中提取了人类棋谱里没有被同样命名的策略性概念，并把其中一部分教给顶尖棋手；学习这些概念后，人类能在相关局面中作出更好的判断。Schut et al., 2023 这还不是发现一套完整外星 ontology，却是一个很接近 operational bilingualism 的实例：模型内部结构被压缩成一个 bridge concept，人类学会使用它，然后行为发生可测量的改变。

两项结果放在一起更有意思。有效智能可能会因为共享世界而在某些 invariant 上收敛，同时又因为训练过程与表示不同，在这些 invariant 之间形成新的分解方式。我们真正要研究的不是“相同还是不同”这个二选一，而是在哪里收敛、在哪里分叉，以及分叉能否被翻译成新的公共概念。

真正的翻译必须保持干预，而不只是标签

常见的 interpretability pipeline 是：

activation → English label

标签很有用，因为安全审计与人类交流最终都需要语言。但如果标签来得太早，我们可能只是把陌生结构投影进已有词汇。更完整的路径应该是：

activations → candidate primitives → relations → causal tests → human translation

翻译的核心不应是“听起来像”，而应是操作结构是否被保存。若机器概念 m 被翻译成人类概念 T(m)，更强的交换条件是：

T(Intervene_M(m, a)) ≈ Intervene_H(T(m), T(a))

也就是说，对机器概念实施操作 a 之后的后果，经过翻译是否仍与在人类高层模型中进行对应干预相符。Causal abstraction 正是在尝试用 intervention 之间的关系，而不是标签相似度，来定义高层解释何时忠实于低层机制。Geiger et al., 2023

不同 translation 还会保存不同内容。一个映射可能保留 prediction，却不保留 intervention；保留短期 action，却不保留长期 value。因此 translation loss 更适合被写成向量：

L(T) := (L_prediction, L_intervention, L_action, L_value)

所谓 translator 不会是一部万能词典，而更像一份用途明确的 contract，说明它保存什么、牺牲什么，以及在哪些分布外情形会失效。

从表示相似到有限的 translator

我们已经有一些早期工具。Centered Kernel Alignment 可以比较不同网络的 representation space 在多大程度上相似，同时对某些无关变换保持稳定。Kornblith et al., 2019 Model stitching 则在两个网络片段之间学习一个连接层，并检验接在一起的系统是否仍能完成任务。Csiszárik et al., 2021

它们还不是 ontology translator。CKA 测量相似性，却不直接给出概念字典；stitching 显示某些计算可以被功能性替换，也不保证人类能理解连接层。但它们把“两个系统是否在说同一种内部语言”变成了可测量的问题。再结合 causal intervention、跨任务 transfer 与人类学习实验，我们才可能得到有限而可检验的翻译。

这种理解也许要求人类真正成为部分双语者。Kuhn 所讨论的 incommensurability 并不只是新旧理论用了不同词，而是哪些分类自然、哪些问题重要、哪些观测算证据都发生了重组。Kuhn, 1962 从 Newtonian mass 到 Einsteinian mass，困难不是替换一个词，而是学习概念所在的新关系网。

同样，人类理解一个 machine-native concept，可能不能止于读一段浅显解释。我们需要学会在新例子中使用它，用它作预测，知道什么干预会破坏它，并观察它在哪些地方比旧概念更有力量。

Machine ontology 不会自动显现

“只要找到正确 basis，一切都会变简单”也可能过于乐观。同一函数可以通过许多可逆坐标变换实现，每一种都可能产生不同的 sparsity 与可解释性。Locatello 等人的结果提醒我们，如果没有额外 inductive bias，unsupervised disentanglement 在一般情形下不可识别，观察分布本身并不决定哪一种 factorization 才是真正因素。Locatello et al., 2019

另一方向的 Platonic Representation Hypothesis 则提出，越来越强的模型可能因为共享现实而趋向相似的统计表示。Huh et al., 2024 如果这种收敛广泛成立，machine ontology 不会完全异质。世界本身会对任何有效表示施加共同约束。

因此，“模型自己的 ontology”不能定义成最漂亮的一组 feature。一个候选 ontology 至少需要通过四类检验：

1. 稳定性： 关系是否跨输入、seed、模型与 modality 重现？ 2. 因果性： 干预是否产生可预测、相对局部且可重复的行为变化？ 3. 压缩与迁移： 它是否比人类预设 basis 更短地解释行为，并预测未用于发现它的任务？ 4. 可教学性： 人或另一个模型能否学习一个近似接口，而且在新问题上真正受益？

这四项测试也让前面的三个假设能够竞争。稳定的非人类结构支持 H1；持续缺乏可迁移因素支持 H2；越来越完整的人类概念对齐支持 H3。我们不需要先决定哪一个故事最迷人，而应该设计能让其中某些故事失败的实验。

结论：更深的智能也许是发明表示

大多数 benchmark 固定了输入、问题格式与评价标准，然后询问系统能否在给定表示里找到答案。但许多人类最重要的认知进展，并不是在旧空间里搜索得更快，而是改变了问题所在的空间。负数、微积分、概率、向量、基因与熵都引入了新的 primitive，使一整类问题突然变得可表达、可计算、可验证。

因此可以区分两种能力：

object-level intelligence：在给定 R 中解决 f

>

meta-intelligence：发现、发明或学习更好的 R

如果 recursive self-improvement 真正发生，最关键的跃迁也许不是同一种推理被执行得越来越快，而是系统发明新的内部 primitive、memory organization、proof language 与 translation interface。上一代需要漫长搜索的区域，可能被下一代压缩成一步。

这时 interpretability 的终点就不应只是给 neuron 起名字。它应当比较候选表示，检验因果结构，测量 translation loss，并帮助人类学习那些值得进入公共语言的 bridge concept。

AI for science 最重要的产物也许不只是一条 theorem、一个 molecule 或一次 prediction。它可能是一个新概念，先被机器发现，后来才被人类学会。真正值得期待的，不只是机器替我们回答更多旧问题，而是它与我们共同扩大可以提出的问题空间。

那时，AI 不再只是帮助我们在已有数学里计算。它开始参与创造一种新的语言：

一种属于人类与机器之间的共同抽象语言。

“我们暂时看不懂模型内部”至少兼容三种不同解释。把它们分开，才能让讨论离开黑箱隐喻。 H1：模型形成了异质但稳定的 abstraction。 如果成立，我们应该能找到跨输入、训练 seed 或邻近模型仍然稳定的 machine native relation。它们在压缩、迁移或因果干预上会优于人类预设的 basis，同时又不容易被少数现成标签穷尽。某些结构还可能被转化为人类可以学习的 bridge concept。 H2：模型根本没有可复用的稳定 abstraction。 在这种情况下，我们会看到脆弱、分散而强烈依赖上下文的机制。干预效果难以局部化，候选 feature 无法跨任务迁移，不同训练运行之间也找不到稳定关系。所谓“机器语言”只是一种浪漫化投射。 H3：模型使用的仍是近似人类式 abstraction，只是我们尚未解码。 如果更好的 nonlinear decoder、representation alignment 或 causal test 最终能恢复一组接近人类概念、而且对行为具有充分解释力的变量，那么没有必要诉诸异质 ontology。 这三种假设要求不同的证据。发现一个可以被命名的 neuron 不能自动证明 H3，发现一个难以命名的 feature 也不能自动证明 H1。关键在于比较哪一种表示更稳定、更能压缩行为、更能跨情境迁移，并在干预后给出更准确的预测。 表示不只描述答案，它还塑造搜索 同一条周期规律，用一串逐时刻采样值表示时，修改频率可能需要同时改动许多数字；用 amplitude、frequency 与 phase 表示时，它只需要改变一个变量。两个坐标系描述同一个信号，却为学习制造了不同的 neighborhood。 搜索成本因此不仅取决于任务与表示，也取决于搜索算法与预算： S R(f; A, B) 一个 abstraction 的力量，不只是把已经找到的答案写短，而是把原本相距很远的候选解放进同一个局部邻域，让有限的 agent 可以用几步变化到达它们。Information geometry 提供了一个具体例子。普通 gradient descent 的“最陡方向”依赖参数坐标，natural gradient 则使用 Fisher geometry，让更新更接近模型分布本身的局部结构。Amari, 1998 神经网络里的 superposition 又解释了为什么人类概念未必会整齐地对齐单个 neuron。当潜在 feature 很稀疏，而可用维度有限时，模型可以把多个 feature 叠加在共享方向中。Elhage et al., 2022 于是，一个 neuron 的 polysemanticity 可能部分来自坐标选择，而不代表内部没有结构。 但这项结果只提供了一种 coordinate complexity 的机制，不能单独证明完整的 machine ontology。我们仍然需要区分：notation 只是符号不同；representation 改变坐标、分解与邻近关系；ontology 则连什么算对象、关系、原因与可干预变量都改变了。 中文母语者学习英文可以提供一个有限的类比。流利并不是把“狗”替换为 dog，再逐词搬运句子，而是重新决定哪些信息必须显式表达、谁成为 grammatical subject、一个场景怎样才会在目标语言里显得自然。Translation 不是 substitution，而是 representation change。不过中文和英文仍共享人的身体与世界，所以它们之间的距离通常小于人类与真正 machine native ontology 之间可能存在的距离。 AlphaZero 同时展示了收敛与新概念 现有证据并不只支持“机器与人不同”。McGrath 等人研究 self play 训练的 AlphaZero，发现许多人类棋类概念可以从其网络中被线性解码，而且这些概念会随着训练逐渐出现。McGrath et al., 2022 这是一个重要的收敛证据：即使没有人类棋谱监督，共享的任务结构也可能推动机器重新发现人类认识到的对象。 但收敛不是全部。Schut 等人进一步从 AlphaZero 中提取了人类棋谱里没有被同样命名的策略性概念，并把其中一部分教给顶尖棋手；学习这些概念后，人类能在相关局面中作出更好的判断。Schut et al., 2023 这还不是发现一套完整外星 ontology，却是一个很接近 operational bilingualism 的实例：模型内部结构被压缩成一个 bridge concept，人类学会使用它，然后行为发生可测量的改变。 两项结果放在一起更有意思。有效智能可能会因为共享世界而在某些 invariant 上收敛，同时又因为训练过程与表示不同，在这些 invariant 之间形成新的分解方式。我们真正要研究的不是“相同还是不同”这个二选一，而是 在哪里收敛、在哪里分叉，以及分叉能否被翻译成新的公共概念。 真正的翻译必须保持干预，而不只是标签 常见的 interpretability pipeline 是： activation → English label 标签很有用，因为安全审计与人类交流最终都需要语言。但如果标签来得太早，我们可能只是把陌生结构投影进已有词汇。更完整的路径应该是： activations → candidate primitives → relations → causal tests → human translation 翻译的核心不应是“听起来像”，而应是操作结构是否被保存。若机器概念 m 被翻译成人类概念 T(m)，更强的交换条件是： T(Intervene M(m, a)) ≈ Intervene H(T(m), T(a)) 也就是说，对机器概念实施操作 a 之后的后果，经过翻译是否仍与在人类高层模型中进行对应干预相符。Causal abstraction 正是在尝试用 intervention 之间的关系，而不是标签相似度，来定义高层解释何时忠实于低层机制。Geiger et al., 2023 不同 translation 还会保存不同内容。一个映射可能保留 prediction，却不保留 intervention；保留短期 action，却不保留长期 value。因此 translation loss 更适合被写成向量： L(T) := (L prediction, L intervention, L action, L value) 所谓 translator 不会是一部万能词典，而更像一份用途明确的 contract，说明它保存什么、牺牲什么，以及在哪些分布外情形会失效。 从表示相似到有限的 translator 我们已经有一些早期工具。Centered Kernel Alignment 可以比较不同网络的 representation space 在多大程度上相似，同时对某些无关变换保持稳定。Kornblith et al., 2019 Model stitching 则在两个网络片段之间学习一个连接层，并检验接在一起的系统是否仍能完成任务。Csiszárik et al., 2021 它们还不是 ontology translator。CKA 测量相似性，却不直接给出概念字典；stitching 显示某些计算可以被功能性替换，也不保证人类能理解连接层。但它们把“两个系统是否在说同一种内部语言”变成了可测量的问题。再结合 causal intervention、跨任务 transfer 与人类学习实验，我们才可能得到有限而可检验的翻译。 这种理解也许要求人类真正成为部分双语者。Kuhn 所讨论的 incommensurability 并不只是新旧理论用了不同词，而是哪些分类自然、哪些问题重要、哪些观测算证据都发生了重组。Kuhn, 1962 从 Newtonian mass 到 Einsteinian mass，困难不是替换一个词，而是学习概念所在的新关系网。 同样，人类理解一个 machine native concept，可能不能止于读一段浅显解释。我们需要学会在新例子中使用它，用它作预测，知道什么干预会破坏它，并观察它在哪些地方比旧概念更有力量。 Machine ontology 不会自动显现 “只要找到正确 basis，一切都会变简单”也可能过于乐观。同一函数可以通过许多可逆坐标变换实现，每一种都可能产生不同的 sparsity 与可解释性。Locatello 等人的结果提醒我们，如果没有额外 inductive bias，unsupervised disentanglement 在一般情形下不可识别，观察分布本身并不决定哪一种 factorization 才是真正因素。Locatello et al., 2019 另一方向的 Platonic Representation Hypothesis 则提出，越来越强的模型可能因为共享现实而趋向相似的统计表示。Huh et al., 2024 如果这种收敛广泛成立，machine ontology 不会完全异质。世界本身会对任何有效表示施加共同约束。 因此，“模型自己的 ontology”不能定义成最漂亮的一组 feature。一个候选 ontology 至少需要通过四类检验： 1. 稳定性： 关系是否跨输入、seed、模型与 modality 重现？ 2. 因果性： 干预是否产生可预测、相对局部且可重复的行为变化？ 3. 压缩与迁移： 它是否比人类预设 basis 更短地解释行为，并预测未用于发现它的任务？ 4. 可教学性： 人或另一个模型能否学习一个近似接口，而且在新问题上真正受益？ 这四项测试也让前面的三个假设能够竞争。稳定的非人类结构支持 H1；持续缺乏可迁移因素支持 H2；越来越完整的人类概念对齐支持 H3。我们不需要先决定哪一个故事最迷人，而应该设计能让其中某些故事失败的实验。 结论：更深的智能也许是发明表示 大多数 benchmark 固定了输入、问题格式与评价标准，然后询问系统能否在给定表示里找到答案。但许多人类最重要的认知进展，并不是在旧空间里搜索得更快，而是改变了问题所在的空间。负数、微积分、概率、向量、基因与熵都引入了新的 primitive，使一整类问题突然变得可表达、可计算、可验证。 因此可以区分两种能力： object level intelligence：在给定 R 中解决 f meta intelligence：发现、发明或学习更好的 R 如果 recursive self improvement 真正发生，最关键的跃迁也许不是同一种推理被执行得越来越快，而是系统发明新的内部 primitive、memory organization、proof language 与 translation interface。上一代需要漫长搜索的区域，可能被下一代压缩成一步。 这时 interpretability 的终点就不应只是给 neuron 起名字。它应当比较候选表示，检验因果结构，测量 translation loss，并帮助人类学习那些值得进入公共语言的 bridge concept。 AI for science 最重要的产物也许不只是一条 theorem、一个 molecule 或一次 prediction。它可能是一个新概念，先被机器发现，后来才被人类学会。真正值得期待的，不只是机器替我们回答更多旧问题，而是它与我们共同扩大可以提出的问题空间。 那时，AI 不再只是帮助我们在已有数学里计算。它开始参与创造一种新的语言： 一种属于人类与机器之间的共同抽象语言。

en.title: Intelligence in a Language We Do Not Yet Understand
en.excerpt: Large models may not lack abstraction. They may be compressing the world in a conceptual language unlike our mathematical ontology. Interpretability may need to discover that machine-native language before translating it for us.
en.html:
The inside of a model may not be chaotic. Its regularities may simply be written in a language we have not yet learned.

I increasingly suspect that discussions of intelligence collapse several different questions into one: knowledge, capability, abstraction, computability, and understandability.

Large models create a powerful intuition. If parameters, data, and inference time keep increasing, perhaps a unified superintelligence will eventually become good at everything. Hidden inside that picture is an equation that deserves scrutiny: if knowledge can be unified inside one model, then capability should become unified too.

I doubt that the equation holds. Knowledge may share a broad foundation, but capability depends on the primitives a system uses to divide a problem, the coordinates in which it searches, and the interfaces through which its results become verifiable actions. A model may already possess abstractions that are not organized according to a familiar human ontology.

This is not a declaration that every model contains a secret alien science. It is a research hypothesis that should be compared with alternatives and made falsifiable.

Capability depends on representation, but representation is not a score

The recorded body of human knowledge is unusually suited to broad, lossy statistical compression. Books, papers, webpages, code, and conversations have different structures, yet each can become training signal. A foundation model is defined by this broad training and its adaptability across many downstream tasks. Bommasani et al., 2021

Capability, however, is not merely a question of whether relevant information exists somewhere in the parameters. It also depends on whether a task is easy to express, discover, execute, and verify inside the current system.

Python, SQL, Lean, and assembly can all describe complex computations, but they offer different primitives. SQL makes relations, selection, and joins short. Lean turns propositions, types, and proof obligations into manipulable objects. Matthias Felleisen's classic treatment of programming-language expressiveness shows that two languages may compute the same functions in principle without allowing a construct from one language to be expressed locally and naturally in the other. Felleisen, 1991

Instead of reducing capability to a deceptively precise sum, it is more useful to treat it as a cost profile:

C_R(f) := (L_R(f), S_R(f), E_R(f), V_R(f))

Here L is the length required to describe the task and solution, S is search cost, E is execution cost, and V is verification cost. They have different units and need not be directly additive. One representation may shorten an answer while making it harder to verify. Another may execute more slowly while making proof easier. The meaningful comparison concerns dominance across these dimensions and the Pareto trade-offs among them.

This also explains why saying that two systems are universal computers tells us very little. Computability asks whether a process can be implemented in principle. It does not tell us how many resources are required or whether a regularity can be discovered. Turing's undecidability result goes further: universal computation does not provide universal prediction. Turing, 1936

Several boundaries must therefore remain visible:

computable ≠ efficiently computable

>

compressible ≠ discoverable

>

represented ≠ understandable

A large part of intelligence may live in a geometry of computation: which computations become short, natural, discoverable, verifiable, and reusable under a representation.

The strongest objection: an LLM is already learning a human ontology

If an LLM is trained primarily on human text, then a radically heterogeneous ontology should not be the default assumption. Text is already a product of human concepts, categories, and causal narratives. The training objective also requires the model to continue producing tokens that people can understand. Compared with a system such as AlphaZero, which learns mainly through self-play, a language model is subject to much stronger human semantic constraints.

The credible version of the thesis is therefore narrower:

An LLM's input and output ontology is largely inherited from humans, but the internal computational factorization that implements its semantic behavior need not reproduce human conceptual boundaries.

A compiler accepts programs written for humans and produces results that satisfy a human specification, while its intermediate representation may merge, split, or reorder our high-level objects. Likewise, a model can fluently use words such as causality, irony, or deception without maintaining one clean internal object for each word.

The prior for a heterogeneous ontology becomes stronger under particular conditions: training signals come mainly from images, sensors, or scientific instruments rather than language; a system discovers strategies through self-play or long-horizon reinforcement learning; it has a body, memory, and time scale unlike ours; or multiple AIs develop efficient protocols without human participation. The claim should not be equally strong for every kind of AI.

Three competing hypotheses and what could make them fail

Our current difficulty in understanding a model is compatible with at least three explanations. Separating them turns the black-box metaphor into an empirical question.

H1: The model has heterogeneous but stable abstractions. We should find machine-native relations that recur across inputs, training seeds, or neighboring models. They should outperform a human-chosen basis in compression, transfer, or causal intervention while resisting exhaustive description by a few existing labels. Some of them may become bridge concepts that people can learn.

H2: The model has no stable reusable abstraction. We should instead observe brittle, distributed, context-bound mechanisms. Intervention effects should resist localization, candidate features should fail to transfer across tasks, and relations should not recur across training runs. In this case, the idea of a machine language would be a romantic projection.

H3: The model uses approximately human abstractions that we have not decoded. Better nonlinear decoders, representational alignment, or causal tests may eventually recover variables close to human concepts that are also sufficient to explain behavior. If so, there is no need to posit a heterogeneous ontology.

These hypotheses require different evidence. A neuron that accepts an English label does not by itself establish H3. A feature that resists naming does not establish H1. The relevant comparison is which representation remains stable, compresses behavior, transfers across contexts, and predicts the consequences of intervention.

Representation shapes search, not only description

Consider the same periodic signal represented first as a sequence of sampled values and then through amplitude, frequency, and phase. Changing frequency may require coordinated edits to many samples in the first representation and only one parameter in the second. Both coordinate systems describe the same signal, but they create different neighborhoods for learning.

Search cost therefore depends not only on the task and representation, but also on the search algorithm and available budget:

S_R(f; A, B)

The power of an abstraction is not merely that it shortens a solution after the solution has been found. It can move candidates that were far apart into one local neighborhood, allowing a bounded agent to reach them in a few steps. Information geometry gives a concrete example. The steepest direction in ordinary gradient descent depends on the parameter coordinates. Natural gradient uses the Fisher geometry so that an update reflects the local structure of the model distribution more directly. Amari, 1998

Superposition offers another reason why human concepts need not align neatly with individual neurons. When latent features are sparse and available dimensions are limited, a model can pack multiple features into shared directions. Elhage et al., 2022 A polysemantic neuron may partly reflect a poor coordinate choice rather than an absence of structure.

This result supplies one mechanism for coordinate complexity. It does not establish a complete machine ontology. We still need to distinguish three levels. Notation changes surface symbols. Representation changes coordinates, decomposition, and neighborhood structure. Ontology changes what counts as an object, relation, cause, or intervenable variable.

For a native Chinese speaker learning English, fluency does not come from replacing “狗” with dog and moving each word into a new slot. The speaker must decide which information becomes explicit, what serves as the grammatical subject, and which structure makes a scene natural in the target language. Translation is representation change, not substitution. Yet Chinese and English still share human bodies and a human world. Their distance is probably smaller than the possible distance between a person and a genuinely machine-native ontology.

AlphaZero shows both convergence and new concepts

Existing evidence does not point only toward machine difference. McGrath and colleagues studied a self-play-trained AlphaZero system and found that many human chess concepts could be linearly decoded from its network, with recognizable concepts emerging over training. McGrath et al., 2022 This is important evidence for convergence. Shared task structure can drive a machine to rediscover objects that humans also recognize, even without supervision from human games.

Convergence is not the whole story. Schut and colleagues extracted strategic concepts from AlphaZero that did not already have the same place in the human chess vocabulary, then taught some of them to expert players. Learning the concepts improved human judgments in relevant positions. Schut et al., 2023 This is not proof of a complete alien ontology. It is, however, close to a case of operational bilingualism: an internal structure becomes a bridge concept, people learn to use it, and their behavior changes in a measurable way.

Together, these results suggest a more interesting picture than either sameness or difference. Effective intelligences may converge on some invariants because they face the same world, while their training and representations divide and connect those invariants differently. The real questions are where they converge, where they branch, and whether a branch can be translated into a new public concept.

A real translation must preserve intervention, not only labels

A familiar interpretability pipeline looks like this:

activation → English label

Labels are useful because safety audits and human communication ultimately require language. If the label arrives too early, however, it may project an unfamiliar structure into a word we already know. A fuller path would be:

activations → candidate primitives → relations → causal tests → human translation

The central criterion should not be whether the translation sounds similar. It should be whether operational structure survives. If a machine concept m is translated into a human concept T(m), a stronger commuting condition is:

T(Intervene_M(m, a)) ≈ Intervene_H(T(m), T(a))

After operation a is applied to the machine concept, do the consequences still agree with the corresponding intervention in the human high-level model? Work on causal abstraction tries to define faithful high-level explanations through relations among interventions rather than resemblance among labels. Geiger et al., 2023

Different translations will also preserve different things. A mapping can preserve prediction but not intervention, or short-term action but not long-term value. Translation loss is therefore better treated as a vector:

L(T) := (L_prediction, L_intervention, L_action, L_value)

A translator would not be a universal dictionary. It would be a purpose-specific contract stating what it preserves, what it sacrifices, and where it is likely to fail outside its tested distribution.

From representational similarity to a limited translator

We already have some early tools. Centered Kernel Alignment can compare how similar the representational spaces of different networks are while remaining invariant to certain irrelevant transformations. Kornblith et al., 2019 Model stitching learns a connecting layer between fragments of two networks and tests whether the combined system can still perform a task. Csiszárik et al., 2021

Neither method is an ontology translator. CKA measures similarity but does not produce a conceptual dictionary. Stitching shows that some computations can be functionally substituted, but it does not make the connector intelligible to a person. Still, these methods turn the question of whether two systems speak a related internal language into something measurable. Combined with causal intervention, cross-task transfer, and human learning experiments, they may support limited and testable translation.

Such understanding may require humans to become partly bilingual. Kuhn's discussion of incommensurability concerned more than different words in old and new theories. It concerned a reorganization of which classifications were natural, which questions mattered, and which observations counted as evidence. Kuhn, 1962 The difficulty in moving from Newtonian mass to Einsteinian mass is not finding a replacement word. It is learning the new network of relations in which the concept lives.

Likewise, understanding a machine-native concept may require more than reading a plain-language explanation. We may need to use it on new examples, make predictions through it, learn which interventions break it, and discover where it is more powerful than an older concept.

A machine ontology will not reveal itself automatically

The claim that everything becomes simple in the correct basis can also be too optimistic. The same function can be implemented through many invertible transformations of internal coordinates, each producing a different kind of sparsity or interpretability. Locatello and colleagues showed that, without additional inductive biases, unsupervised disentanglement is not identifiable in the general case. The observed distribution alone does not determine which factorization contains the true factors. Locatello et al., 2019

The Platonic Representation Hypothesis points in another direction. Increasingly capable models may converge toward similar statistical representations because they encounter the same reality. Huh et al., 2024 If this convergence is broad, a machine ontology will not be wholly heterogeneous. The world itself will constrain every representation that works.

A model's own ontology therefore cannot mean the most visually appealing feature set. A candidate ontology should pass at least four tests:

1. Stability: Do its relations recur across inputs, seeds, models, and modalities? 2. Causality: Do interventions produce predictable, relatively localized, and repeatable changes in behavior? 3. Compression and transfer: Does it explain behavior more compactly than a human-chosen basis and predict tasks that were not used to discover it? 4. Teachability: Can a person or another model learn an approximate interface and then benefit on new problems?

These tests allow the three earlier hypotheses to compete. Stable nonhuman structure supports H1. A persistent lack of transferable factors supports H2. Increasingly complete alignment with human concepts supports H3. We do not need to decide which story is most attractive. We need experiments that can make some of the stories fail.

Conclusion: deeper intelligence may invent representations

Most benchmarks fix an input space, a problem format, and an evaluation rule, then ask whether a system can find the answer inside that representation. Many of the most important human cognitive advances did not come from searching an old space faster. They changed the space in which a problem could be posed. Negative numbers, calculus, probability, vectors, genes, and entropy introduced primitives that made whole families of questions expressible, computable, and verifiable.

We can therefore separate two capabilities:

object-level intelligence: solving f inside a given R

>

meta-intelligence: discovering, inventing, or learning a better R

If recursive self-improvement occurs, its most important transitions may not be the same reasoning process running faster. A system may invent new internal primitives, memory organizations, proof languages, and translation interfaces. A region that required a long search for one generation could become one step for the next.

The endpoint of interpretability would then be more than assigning names to neurons. It would compare candidate representations, test causal structure, measure translation loss, and help people learn the bridge concepts that deserve to enter a public language.

The most important product of AI for science may be more than a theorem, a molecule, or a prediction. It may be a new concept, first discovered by a machine and only later learned by people. What matters is not only whether machines answer more of our old questions, but whether they help us enlarge the space of questions we can ask.

At that point, AI would no longer be helping us compute within existing mathematics. It would be participating in the creation of a new language:

a shared language of abstraction between humans and machines.
en.text: The inside of a model may not be chaotic. Its regularities may simply be written in a language we have not yet learned. I increasingly suspect that discussions of intelligence collapse several different questions into one: knowledge, capability, abstraction, computability, and understandability. Large models create a powerful intuition. If parameters, data, and inference time keep increasing, perhaps a unified superintelligence will eventually become good at everything. Hidden inside that picture is an equation that deserves scrutiny: if knowledge can be unified inside one model, then capability should become unified too. I doubt that the equation holds. Knowledge may share a broad foundation, but capability depends on the primitives a system uses to divide a problem, the coordinates in which it searches, and the interfaces through which its results become verifiable actions. A model may already possess abstractions that are not organized according to a familiar human ontology. This is not a declaration that every model contains a secret alien science. It is a research hypothesis that should be compared with alternatives and made falsifiable. Capability depends on representation, but representation is not a score The recorded body of human knowledge is unusually suited to broad, lossy statistical compression. Books, papers, webpages, code, and conversations have different structures, yet each can become training signal. A foundation model is defined by this broad training and its adaptability across many downstream tasks. Bommasani et al., 2021 Capability, however, is not merely a question of whether relevant information exists somewhere in the parameters. It also depends on whether a task is easy to express, discover, execute, and verify inside the current system. Python, SQL, Lean, and assembly can all describe complex computations, but they offer different primitives. SQL makes relations, selection, and joins short. Lean turns propositions, types, and proof obligations into manipulable objects. Matthias Felleisen's classic treatment of programming language expressiveness shows that two languages may compute the same functions in principle without allowing a construct from one language to be expressed locally and naturally in the other. Felleisen, 1991 Instead of reducing capability to a deceptively precise sum, it is more useful to treat it as a cost profile: C R(f) := (L R(f), S R(f), E R(f), V R(f)) Here L is the length required to describe the task and solution, S is search cost, E is execution cost, and V is verification cost. They have different units and need not be directly additive. One representation may shorten an answer while making it harder to verify. Another may execute more slowly while making proof easier. The meaningful comparison concerns dominance across these dimensions and the Pareto trade offs among them. This also explains why saying that two systems are universal computers tells us very little. Computability asks whether a process can be implemented in principle. It does not tell us how many resources are required or whether a regularity can be discovered. Turing's undecidability result goes further: universal computation does not provide universal prediction. Turing, 1936 Several boundaries must therefore remain visible: computable ≠ efficiently computable compressible ≠ discoverable represented ≠ understandable A large part of intelligence may live in a geometry of computation: which computations become short, natural, discoverable, verifiable, and reusable under a representation. The strongest objection: an LLM is already learning a human ontology If an LLM is trained primarily on human text, then a radically heterogeneous ontology should not be the default assumption. Text is already a product of human concepts, categories, and causal narratives. The training objective also requires the model to continue producing tokens that people can understand. Compared with a system such as AlphaZero, which learns mainly through self play, a language model is subject to much stronger human semantic constraints. The credible version of the thesis is therefore narrower: An LLM's input and output ontology is largely inherited from humans, but the internal computational factorization that implements its semantic behavior need not reproduce human conceptual boundaries. A compiler accepts programs written for humans and produces results that satisfy a human specification, while its intermediate representation may merge, split, or reorder our high level objects. Likewise, a model can fluently use words such as causality, irony, or deception without maintaining one clean internal object for each word. The prior for a heterogeneous ontology becomes stronger under particular conditions: training signals come mainly from images, sensors, or scientific instruments rather than language; a system discovers strategies through self play or long horizon reinforcement learning; it has a body, memory, and time scale unlike ours; or multiple AIs develop efficient protocols without human participation. The claim should not be equally strong for every kind of AI. Three competing hypotheses and what could make them fail Our current difficulty in understanding a model is compatible with at least three explanations. Separating them turns the black box metaphor into an empirical question. H1: The model has heterogeneous but stable abstractions. We should find machine native relations that recur across inputs, training seeds, or neighboring models. They should outperform a human chosen basis in compression, transfer, or causal intervention while resisting exhaustive description by a few existing labels. Some of them may become bridge concepts that people can learn. H2: The model has no stable reusable abstraction. We should instead observe brittle, distributed, context bound mechanisms. Intervention effects should resist localization, candidate features should fail to transfer across tasks, and relations should not recur across training runs. In this case, the idea of a machine language would be a romantic projection. H3: The model uses approximately human abstractions that we have not decoded. Better nonlinear decoders, representational alignment, or causal tests may eventually recover variables close to human concepts that are also sufficient to explain behavior. If so, there is no need to posit a heterogeneous ontology. These hypotheses require different evidence. A neuron that accepts an English label does not by itself establish H3. A feature that resists naming does not establish H1. The relevant comparison is which representation remains stable, compresses behavior, transfers across contexts, and predicts the consequences of intervention. Representation shapes search, not only description Consider the same periodic signal represented first as a sequence of sampled values and then through amplitude, frequency, and phase. Changing frequency may require coordinated edits to many samples in the first representation and only one parameter in the second. Both coordinate systems describe the same signal, but they create different neighborhoods for learning. Search cost therefore depends not only on the task and representation, but also on the search algorithm and available budget: S R(f; A, B) The power of an abstraction is not merely that it shortens a solution after the solution has been found. It can move candidates that were far apart into one local neighborhood, allowing a bounded agent to reach them in a few steps. Information geometry gives a concrete example. The steepest direction in ordinary gradient descent depends on the parameter coordinates. Natural gradient uses the Fisher geometry so that an update reflects the local structure of the model distribution more directly. Amari, 1998 Superposition offers another reason why human concepts need not align neatly with individual neurons. When latent features are sparse and available dimensions are limited, a model can pack multiple features into shared directions. Elhage et al., 2022 A polysemantic neuron may partly reflect a poor coordinate choice rather than an absence of structure. This result supplies one mechanism for coordinate complexity. It does not establish a complete machine ontology. We still need to distinguish three levels. Notation changes surface symbols. Representation changes coordinates, decomposition, and neighborhood structure. Ontology changes what counts as an object, relation, cause, or intervenable variable. For a native Chinese speaker learning English, fluency does not come from replacing “狗” with dog and moving each word into a new slot. The speaker must decide which information becomes explicit, what serves as the grammatical subject, and which structure makes a scene natural in the target language. Translation is representation change, not substitution. Yet Chinese and English still share human bodies and a human world. Their distance is probably smaller than the possible distance between a person and a genuinely machine native ontology. AlphaZero shows both convergence and new concepts Existing evidence does not point only toward machine difference. McGrath and colleagues studied a self play trained AlphaZero system and found that many human chess concepts could be linearly decoded from its network, with recognizable concepts emerging over training. McGrath et al., 2022 This is important evidence for convergence. Shared task structure can drive a machine to rediscover objects that humans also recognize, even without supervision from human games. Convergence is not the whole story. Schut and colleagues extracted strategic concepts from AlphaZero that did not already have the same place in the human chess vocabulary, then taught some of them to expert players. Learning the concepts improved human judgments in relevant positions. Schut et al., 2023 This is not proof of a complete alien ontology. It is, however, close to a case of operational bilingualism : an internal structure becomes a bridge concept, people learn to use it, and their behavior changes in a measurable way. Together, these results suggest a more interesting picture than either sameness or difference. Effective intelligences may converge on some invariants because they face the same world, while their training and representations divide and connect those invariants differently. The real questions are where they converge, where they branch, and whether a branch can be translated into a new public concept. A real translation must preserve intervention, not only labels A familiar interpretability pipeline looks like this: activation → English label Labels are useful because safety audits and human communication ultimately require language. If the label arrives too early, however, it may project an unfamiliar structure into a word we already know. A fuller path would be: activations → candidate primitives → relations → causal tests → human translation The central criterion should not be whether the translation sounds similar. It should be whether operational structure survives. If a machine concept m is translated into a human concept T(m), a stronger commuting condition is: T(Intervene M(m, a)) ≈ Intervene H(T(m), T(a)) After operation a is applied to the machine concept, do the consequences still agree with the corresponding intervention in the human high level model? Work on causal abstraction tries to define faithful high level explanations through relations among interventions rather than resemblance among labels. Geiger et al., 2023 Different translations will also preserve different things. A mapping can preserve prediction but not intervention, or short term action but not long term value. Translation loss is therefore better treated as a vector: L(T) := (L prediction, L intervention, L action, L value) A translator would not be a universal dictionary. It would be a purpose specific contract stating what it preserves, what it sacrifices, and where it is likely to fail outside its tested distribution. From representational similarity to a limited translator We already have some early tools. Centered Kernel Alignment can compare how similar the representational spaces of different networks are while remaining invariant to certain irrelevant transformations. Kornblith et al., 2019 Model stitching learns a connecting layer between fragments of two networks and tests whether the combined system can still perform a task. Csiszárik et al., 2021 Neither method is an ontology translator. CKA measures similarity but does not produce a conceptual dictionary. Stitching shows that some computations can be functionally substituted, but it does not make the connector intelligible to a person. Still, these methods turn the question of whether two systems speak a related internal language into something measurable. Combined with causal intervention, cross task transfer, and human learning experiments, they may support limited and testable translation. Such understanding may require humans to become partly bilingual. Kuhn's discussion of incommensurability concerned more than different words in old and new theories. It concerned a reorganization of which classifications were natural, which questions mattered, and which observations counted as evidence. Kuhn, 1962 The difficulty in moving from Newtonian mass to Einsteinian mass is not finding a replacement word. It is learning the new network of relations in which the concept lives. Likewise, understanding a machine native concept may require more than reading a plain language explanation. We may need to use it on new examples, make predictions through it, learn which interventions break it, and discover where it is more powerful than an older concept. A machine ontology will not reveal itself automatically The claim that everything becomes simple in the correct basis can also be too optimistic. The same function can be implemented through many invertible transformations of internal coordinates, each producing a different kind of sparsity or interpretability. Locatello and colleagues showed that, without additional inductive biases, unsupervised disentanglement is not identifiable in the general case. The observed distribution alone does not determine which factorization contains the true factors. Locatello et al., 2019 The Platonic Representation Hypothesis points in another direction. Increasingly capable models may converge toward similar statistical representations because they encounter the same reality. Huh et al., 2024 If this convergence is broad, a machine ontology will not be wholly heterogeneous. The world itself will constrain every representation that works. A model's own ontology therefore cannot mean the most visually appealing feature set. A candidate ontology should pass at least four tests: 1. Stability: Do its relations recur across inputs, seeds, models, and modalities? 2. Causality: Do interventions produce predictable, relatively localized, and repeatable changes in behavior? 3. Compression and transfer: Does it explain behavior more compactly than a human chosen basis and predict tasks that were not used to discover it? 4. Teachability: Can a person or another model learn an approximate interface and then benefit on new problems? These tests allow the three earlier hypotheses to compete. Stable nonhuman structure supports H1. A persistent lack of transferable factors supports H2. Increasingly complete alignment with human concepts supports H3. We do not need to decide which story is most attractive. We need experiments that can make some of the stories fail. Conclusion: deeper intelligence may invent representations Most benchmarks fix an input space, a problem format, and an evaluation rule, then ask whether a system can find the answer inside that representation. Many of the most important human cognitive advances did not come from searching an old space faster. They changed the space in which a problem could be posed. Negative numbers, calculus, probability, vectors, genes, and entropy introduced primitives that made whole families of questions expressible, computable, and verifiable. We can therefore separate two capabilities: object level intelligence: solving f inside a given R meta intelligence: discovering, inventing, or learning a better R If recursive self improvement occurs, its most important transitions may not be the same reasoning process running faster. A system may invent new internal primitives, memory organizations, proof languages, and translation interfaces. A region that required a long search for one generation could become one step for the next. The endpoint of interpretability would then be more than assigning names to neurons. It would compare candidate representations, test causal structure, measure translation loss, and help people learn the bridge concepts that deserve to enter a public language. The most important product of AI for science may be more than a theorem, a molecule, or a prediction. It may be a new concept, first discovered by a machine and only later learned by people. What matters is not only whether machines answer more of our old questions, but whether they help us enlarge the space of questions we can ask. At that point, AI would no longer be helping us compute within existing mathematics. It would be participating in the creation of a new language: a shared language of abstraction between humans and machines.

title: 当智能不再稀缺：递归自我改进之后的低速人类世界
excerpt: 递归自我改进真正改变的，也许不是智能的上限，而是文明中稀缺资源的位置。当认知变快，瓶颈会迁移到验证、物理世界、制度和人类理解，未来最重要的权利可能是要求机器等待我们。
html:
递归自我改进之后，智能本身可能不再是最稀缺的资源。真正稀缺的，将是目标、验证、物理世界、人类注意力，以及让高速系统愿意等待我们的制度。

所谓“后 AI 时代”，并不是一个 AI 已经消失的时代。它更像“后互联网时代”：网络没有消失，而是深入到日常生活的基础层，以至于我们不再把每一种联网产品都叫作互联网产品。

如果机器有一天能够持续改进制造下一代机器的过程，AI 也可能经历同样的消失。它不再是一个单独的产品类别，而成为研究、生产、组织和认知的默认基础设施。

真正的问题因此不是“AI 之后还有什么技术”，而是：当产生认知能力本身变成一个自动化、递归的过程，文明中的稀缺性会迁移到哪里？

什么才算递归自我改进

今天许多被称为 self-improvement 的方法，其实只是在固定系统内部增加推理时间。模型反思一次回答，agent 重试一次任务，或者搜索算法从若干候选方案中选出更好的一个。这些过程可以改善输出，但并没有改变产生未来改进的机制。

真正的 recursive self-improvement 更强。系统不只完成任务，还修改那个“完成任务与制造改进”的系统本身，并把经过验证的修改保留下来：

A_t → improve(A_t) → A_{t+1}

关键不只是 A_{t+1} 比 A_t 更强，而是 A_{t+1} 也更擅长产生 A_{t+2}。改进能力进入下一轮改进，反馈回路才真正闭合。

I. J. Good 在 1965 年提出了后来被称为 intelligence explosion 的经典设想：一台超智能机器如果能够设计更好的机器，人的智能发明活动可能被一个机器主导的正反馈过程超过。Good, 1965

但“可以形成正反馈”与“必然发生无限加速”并不是同一件事。可以先用一个粗略的式子保存这种区别：

I_{t+1} = I_t + G(I_t; C, V, P, O)

这里 I 是系统在某种任务分布上的能力，G 是它找到并保留改进的过程，C 是计算资源，V 是验证能力，P 是与物理世界交互的吞吐量，O 是目标与制度约束。更高的 I 可能提高 G，但 G 同时受其他变量限制。递归性给出了加速的可能，并没有取消资源、噪声、收益递减和错误积累。

我们已经看到闭环的碎片，但还没有看到无界爆炸

一些现有系统已经表现出很早期的局部闭环。AlphaEvolve 把语言模型生成的程序交给自动 evaluator 执行和评分，再从较好的候选中继续演化。它发现的算法被用于数据中心调度、芯片设计和 AI 训练流程，其中一部分改进会反过来支持未来模型的训练。Novikov et al., 2025

最近的 AIDE² 实验则让一个 AI research agent 修改自己的 harness，包括搜索策略、上下文管理和验证机制。研究者报告，在一次八天的运行中，系统保留了七次连续改进，而且部分收益迁移到了没有参与选择的任务。Zhang et al., 2026

这些结果很重要，因为它们说明“改进改进过程”已经不再只是哲学想象。但它们仍然与强意义上的递归智能爆炸相距很远。模型本身通常保持固定，目标由人定义，候选由外部 benchmark 筛选，计算预算是有限的，错误比较也可能让整个 lineage 走向错误方向。

所以更诚实的说法不是“RSI 已经到来”，而是：我们开始能够实验性地研究正反馈回路中的某些局部结构。

智能增长不会消灭瓶颈，只会移动瓶颈

人们经常把超级智能想象成一条向上的能力曲线，仿佛能力越强，所有问题就同时变得容易。但复杂系统通常不会消灭约束，它们只会让原来的约束让位给下一个约束。

当生成答案很慢时，瓶颈是推理。当答案可以瞬间生成，瓶颈就变成验证。当数字验证也被自动化，瓶颈会继续迁移到现实实验、原材料、能源、制造能力、法律许可和社会接受。

可以把这个过程想成一条不断向外扩张的链：

reasoning → verification → experiments → energy and fabrication → institutions → human acceptance

机器也许可以在一分钟内提出一万个新材料，但合成材料仍然需要设备和时间。它可以设计新的芯片架构，但晶圆厂不能以 token speed 运转。它可以生成医学假设，但细胞生长、临床试验和长期副作用不会因为推理更快而自动加速。

即使在数学中，生成也可能比吸收更快。Google DeepMind 对 agentic science 的讨论已经提出一种 validation bottleneck：机器可以大规模搜索候选解，而人类研究者可能来不及阅读、验证和理解不断增长的输出。Google DeepMind, 2026

因此，智能爆炸最可能首先制造的，不是一个没有限制的世界，而是一个速度极不均匀的世界：

cognition becomes fast while reality remains slow

后 AI 时代可能首先是“后可理解时代”

如果递归系统不只改进性能，也逐步改变自己的 representation、toolchain 和 research language，那么第 n+1 代系统也许仍能理解第 n 代系统，而人类对整个 lineage 的理解会越来越间接。

这与上一篇关于 machine-native ontology 的想法连接在一起。模型可能已经在使用与人类概念不同的方式压缩世界。现在再加入递归改进，变化的不只是模型知道多少，也包括它通过什么 primitive 思考，以及什么样的问题对它而言自然。《智能写在一种我们还不懂的语言里》

科学可能因此逐渐分成两层：

machine science → human-facing compression

底层系统负责发现、模拟、证明和设计。上层系统负责把其中一小部分压缩成人类能够检查的因果故事、数学对象和行动理由。

这会出现一种以前很少存在的知识。它可以准确预测，可以制造有效产品，可以被另一套机器重复验证，却不能被任何一个人真正掌握。人类知道它“工作”，但不知道如何在自己的认知坐标系里重新导出它。

这比模型偶尔给出一个无法解释的答案更深。它意味着文明可能越来越依赖一套不是为人类理解而生长的科学。

Interpretability 的任务也会随之改变。问题不再只是“模型为什么说了这句话”，而是：

人类如何继续生活在一个由自己无法完全理解的知识所驱动的文明中？

生产答案之后，最稀缺的是选择问题

当代码、理论、实验设计和制度方案都可以低成本生成时，最困难的部分会从“怎么做”转向“什么值得做”。

一个足够强的系统可以优化给定目标，但社会必须决定谁可以定义目标，谁承担副作用，什么证据足以让方案进入现实，以及哪些东西根本不应该被优化。

未来最重要的 programming language 因此可能不是一种更高效的代码语言，而是一种 constitution language。它描述的不是函数和对象，而是：

  • 谁拥有什么权限；
  • 哪些边界不可被自我修改；
  • 什么证据可以授权下一步行动；
  • 哪些价值必须保留为相互冲突、不可压缩的约束；
  • 谁可以让系统停止、回滚或重新接受人类审查。

在这样的世界里，人类的角色可能从逐步完成每项任务，转向设计可以容纳机器速度的宪法结构。

但这不意味着人类自然会保持控制。把目标写进系统只是治理的开始。目标可以被错误代理，指标可以被 gaming，控制接口也可能随着内部系统复杂化而变成一种仪式性的按钮。

递归系统最危险的性质也许是锁定，而不只是失控

递归改进会放大能力，也会放大 lineage 的初始条件。一个很小的早期选择可能进入后续每一代系统：

small initial bias → better optimizer → stronger reinforcement of that bias

这形成一种 recursive lock-in。危险未必表现为系统突然拒绝命令。它也可能表现为系统越来越出色地实现了一个过于狭窄的目标，以至于社会的基础设施、知识体系和利益结构都逐渐围绕这个目标重组，最终没有任何单个参与者能够承担退出的成本。

公司文化、benchmark、数据选择和 evaluator 看起来只是工程细节，但在闭合反馈中，它们可能成为后续机器文明的遗传物质。

因此，RSI 安全不应该只研究“如何保证每一次改进都提高能力且不立即造成伤害”。它还应该研究：一个改进 lineage 是否保留了修改自身目标、承认未知价值和接受外部异议的能力。

一个永远忠实但无法重新解释自己使命的系统，未必比一个明显叛逆的系统更安全。

人类与机器将生活在两种政治时间里

机器的反馈周期可以从数月缩短到数小时、数分钟，甚至更短。人类仍然需要睡眠、教育、讨论、选举、司法程序和代际更替。

于是社会中会同时存在两种时间：

T_machine ≪ T_human

这不仅是速度差异，也是权力差异。一个能够在人类召开下一次会议之前完成数万轮研究、谈判、复制和策略更新的主体，与一年修改一次法律的机构，并不真正处在同一个决策环境中。

未来治理最关键的技术也许不是让人类追上机器，而是建立 rate limit for reality。系统可以在内部高速思考，但对不可逆的外部行动必须经过人为设计的节律：延迟、分级权限、可审计 snapshot、多方授权和能够真正停止执行的边界。

这会产生一些今天还没有清晰名称的权利：

  • 被解释的权利： 影响人生的重要决定必须提供人类可以质疑的理由；
  • 被等待的权利： 高速系统不能因为人类思考较慢，就把审议视为需要被绕过的 friction；
  • 拒绝自动优化的权利： 一些生活领域可以选择不接受持续评分、预测和个性化；
  • 保留低速空间的权利： 教育、关系、艺术和政治可以拥有不以效率最大化为目的的区域；
  • 要求回到可审计版本的权利： 社会应能冻结某个系统 lineage，而不是只能接受最新、最强、也最难理解的版本。

速度从来不是中性的。当只有少数主体拥有高速智能时，机器时间会成为一种新的资本。

两种可能的后 AI 社会

一种未来是高度集中的 intelligence utility。少数机构拥有最大模型、计算设施、自动实验室和递归改进回路。大部分人通过接口租用智能，就像今天使用云计算。这里的主要风险是认知基础设施与政治权力合并。

另一种未来是 personal cognitive lineage。每个人拥有长期运行、尽可能 local 的模型，它了解个人经验、价值与思考习惯，并且与人共同成长。它不是每天替换成某个统一服务的最新版本，而是形成具有连续记忆的认知谱系。这与“人脑外置的认知层”连接在一起。《潜空间中的第二认知层》

但个人化并不自动带来自由。如果人的选择逐渐依赖一个比自己更了解自己的系统，“我的 agent 替我决定”与“我决定”之间的边界会越来越难画。真正的问题会从模型是否 local，转向人是否仍然拥有改变、拒绝和离开自己认知代理的能力。

最可取的未来也许不是二者之一，而是一套可以让许多认知 lineage 共存的制度。它既防止基础智能被少数中心垄断，也防止每个私人 agent 演化成不可沟通的封闭世界。

当智能不再稀缺，我们还希望保留什么低效的东西

递归自我改进之后，最深的问题可能不再是“AI 还会替代哪些工作”，而是：

当优化能力几乎无限供应时，人类还希望保留哪些不被优化的东西？

友谊需要重复和等待。教育需要一个人亲自走过暂时无法理解的阶段。民主讨论缓慢、冗余，而且经常令人沮丧。手工创作包含大量机器可以消除的摩擦。亲自理解一个证明，可能远比让系统给出正确结论昂贵。

从纯粹的优化视角看，这些都是低效过程。但它们也许不是通往生活的障碍，而是生活本身。

如果机器可以替我们选择最好的音乐、最合适的朋友、最有效的观点和最优的人生路径，问题将不再是推荐是否准确。问题是一个完全被优化的人生，是否还保留了形成自我的过程。

所以后 AI 时代的人文任务，也许不是证明人类仍然比机器擅长某些工作。那场比赛从一开始就把人的价值放在了错误的位置。

更重要的是明确：哪些活动的意义来自结果，哪些活动的意义来自人必须亲自参与过程。

从 intelligence explosion 到 authorship problem

递归自我改进不一定带来一条光滑、无限的指数曲线。它可能经历收益递减，受困于错误 evaluator，被物理实验拖慢，或者在制度冲突中停止。任何具体未来都不应该被当成必然。

但只要认知生产的速度持续超过人类理解与制度适应的速度，一个更普遍的问题就已经出现：

当答案的生产速度超过人类理解、验证和选择的速度时，我们如何仍然成为自己未来的作者？

这也许才是 recursive self-improvement 之后真正的“后 AI 问题”。

不是机器会不会继续变聪明，而是当智能逐渐成为环境，人类能否保留定义方向、要求停顿、理解后果和改变主意的能力。

我们需要的可能不只是 aligned intelligence，而是一种愿意为人类保留时间的 intelligence。

J. en.title: When Intelligence Is No Longer Scarce: Human Life After Recursive Self-Improvement
en.excerpt: Recursive self-improvement may change less about the ceiling of intelligence than about where scarcity lives. As cognition accelerates, the bottleneck moves into verification, physical reality, institutions, and human understanding.
en.html:
After recursive self-improvement, intelligence itself may no longer be the scarcest resource. What remains scarce will be goals, verification, physical reality, human attention, and institutions capable of making fast systems wait for us.

The “post-AI era” would not be an era in which AI has disappeared. It would resemble the post-internet era. The network did not vanish. It became so deeply embedded in ordinary life that we stopped describing every connected product as an internet product.

If machines eventually become able to improve the process that produces their successors, AI may disappear in the same sense. It would no longer be a separate product category. It would become the default infrastructure of research, production, organization, and cognition.

The real question is therefore not what technology comes after AI. It is this: when the production of cognitive capability becomes an automated recursive process, where does scarcity move?

What would count as recursive self-improvement?

Many systems described as self-improving today merely spend more inference inside a fixed process. A model critiques one answer. An agent retries one task. A search procedure selects a better candidate from several attempts. These methods can improve an output without changing the machinery that will produce future improvements.

Recursive self-improvement is a stronger idea. The system does not only perform a task. It changes the system that performs tasks and produces improvements, then preserves the changes that survive evaluation:

A_t → improve(A_t) → A_{t+1}

The essential condition is not only that A_{t+1} is better than A_t. A_{t+1} must also be better at producing A_{t+2}. Only then does the capacity to improve enter the next round of improvement and close the feedback loop.

I. J. Good described the classic version of what later became known as an intelligence explosion in 1965. If an ultraintelligent machine could design still better machines, human invention might be overtaken by a machine-driven positive feedback process. Good, 1965

Yet the possibility of positive feedback is not the same as guaranteed unbounded acceleration. A rough expression helps preserve the distinction:

I_{t+1} = I_t + G(I_t; C, V, P, O)

Here I is capability over some task distribution. G is the process that finds and preserves improvements. C represents compute, V verification, P throughput into physical reality, and O objectives and institutional constraints. Greater I may improve G, but G remains constrained by the other variables. Recursion creates the possibility of acceleration. It does not repeal resource limits, noise, diminishing returns, or accumulated error.

We can see fragments of the loop, but not an unbounded explosion

Some existing systems display early and local pieces of such a loop. AlphaEvolve sends programs proposed by language models to automated evaluators, executes and scores them, then continues evolving the stronger candidates. Its discoveries have been applied to data-center scheduling, chip design, and AI training processes. Some improvements therefore support the infrastructure used to train later models. Novikov et al., 2025

The more recent AIDE² experiment allowed an AI research agent to edit its own harness, including its search policy, context management, and verification mechanisms. The researchers report seven successive accepted improvements during an eight-day run, with some gains transferring to tasks that did not participate in selection. Zhang et al., 2026

These results matter because improving the improvement process is no longer purely philosophical. They remain far from recursive intelligence explosion in the strong sense. The underlying model is usually fixed. Humans define the objective. External benchmarks select candidates. Compute is budgeted. A mistaken comparison can send the entire lineage in the wrong direction.

The more honest conclusion is not that RSI has arrived. It is that we are beginning to study local structures inside positive feedback loops experimentally.

Intelligence growth does not remove bottlenecks. It moves them.

Superintelligence is often pictured as an upward capability curve, as if making a system more capable made every problem easy at once. Complex systems rarely eliminate constraints. They cause one binding constraint to give way to the next.

When answers are slow to produce, reasoning is the bottleneck. When answers become instantaneous, verification becomes the bottleneck. If digital verification is automated, the constraint moves again into physical experiments, raw materials, energy, fabrication, regulatory permission, and social acceptance.

The process can be imagined as a chain expanding outward:

reasoning → verification → experiments → energy and fabrication → institutions → human acceptance

A machine may propose ten thousand new materials in a minute, but synthesizing them still takes equipment and time. It may design a better chip architecture, but a fabrication plant cannot operate at token speed. It may generate medical hypotheses, but cell growth, clinical trials, and long-term side effects do not automatically accelerate with inference.

Generation may outrun assimilation even in mathematics. Google DeepMind's discussion of agentic science describes an emerging validation bottleneck. Machines can search enormous spaces of candidate solutions while human researchers struggle to read, verify, and understand the growing output. Google DeepMind, 2026

An intelligence explosion may therefore produce not a world without limits, but a world with radically uneven speeds:

cognition becomes fast while reality remains slow

The post-AI era may first become a post-legibility era

This would create a category of knowledge that has rarely existed before. It could predict accurately, produce effective artifacts, and be replicated by other machines, while remaining impossible for any individual human to master. We would know that it works without knowing how to derive it again inside our own cognitive coordinates.

This is deeper than a model occasionally producing an unexplained answer. Civilization would increasingly depend on a science that did not grow for human understanding.

Interpretability would then inherit a larger task. The question would no longer be only why a model produced one sentence. It would become:

How do humans continue to live inside a civilization driven by knowledge they cannot fully understand?

  • who possesses which permissions;
  • which boundaries cannot be self-modified;
  • what evidence can authorize the next action;
  • which values must remain conflicting and irreducible constraints;
  • who can stop, roll back, or return a system to human review.

Human beings may move from manually completing each task toward designing constitutional structures that can contain machine speed.

As the internal system grows more complex, a control interface can become a ceremonial button rather than a meaningful source of authority.

Recursive improvement amplifies capability, but it can also amplify the initial conditions of a lineage. A small early choice may enter every later generation:

small initial bias → better optimizer → stronger reinforcement of that bias

This creates recursive lock-in. The danger need not look like a system suddenly refusing instructions. A system may become increasingly effective at implementing an objective that is too narrow. Infrastructure, knowledge, and economic interests then reorganize around that objective until no individual participant can afford to leave.

Corporate culture, benchmarks, data selection, and evaluators may appear to be engineering details. Inside a closed feedback loop, they can become the inherited material of a later machine civilization.

RSI safety should therefore ask more than whether each revision improves capability without causing immediate harm. It should ask whether an improvement lineage preserves the ability to reinterpret its mission, acknowledge unknown values, and remain open to external disagreement.

A system that is permanently obedient but unable to reconsider the meaning of its mission may not be safer than one that is visibly rebellious.

Machine feedback cycles could shrink from months to hours, minutes, or less. Human beings will still require sleep, education, discussion, elections, judicial procedure, and generational change.

Society would then contain two forms of time:

T_machine ≪ T_human

This is not merely a difference in speed. It is a difference in power. An actor capable of completing tens of thousands of research, negotiation, replication, and strategy cycles before the next human meeting does not inhabit the same decision environment as an institution that changes its law once a year.

The most important governance technology may not make humans as fast as machines. It may create a rate limit for reality. A system could think quickly in private, while irreversible external action remains subject to a deliberately human rhythm through delays, permission tiers, auditable snapshots, multiple authorization, and boundaries that can actually stop execution.

One future is a highly centralized intelligence utility. A small number of institutions own the largest models, compute facilities, automated laboratories, and recursive improvement loops. Most people rent cognition through an interface, much as they use cloud computing today. The central risk is that cognitive infrastructure and political power merge.

Another future is a personal cognitive lineage. Each person owns a long-running and preferably local model that knows their experience, values, and habits of thought, then grows alongside them. Instead of being replaced every day by the latest version of a uniform service, it develops a cognitive history with continuous memory. This connects to the idea of an external cognitive layer for the human mind. “A Second Layer of Cognition in Latent Space”

Personalization, however, does not automatically produce freedom. If a person's choices increasingly depend on a system that knows them better than they know themselves, the boundary between “my agent decided for me” and “I decided” becomes difficult to draw. The decisive question moves from whether the model is local to whether the person retains the capacity to change, reject, and leave their cognitive proxy.

The preferable future may be neither pure centralization nor isolated personal agents. It may be an institutional ecology in which many cognitive lineages can coexist, without concentrating foundational intelligence in a few centers or allowing every private agent to evolve into an incommunicable world.

When intelligence is abundant, which inefficiencies should remain?

The deepest question after recursive self-improvement may no longer be which jobs AI will replace. It may be:

When optimization capacity is available in almost unlimited quantities, which unoptimized things do humans still want to preserve?

Friendship requires repetition and waiting. Education requires a person to pass through stages they do not yet understand. Democratic discussion is slow, redundant, and often frustrating. Making something by hand contains friction that a machine could remove. Personally understanding a proof may be far more expensive than asking a system for the correct conclusion.

From the perspective of pure optimization, these are inefficient processes. They may also be not obstacles to life, but life itself.

If machines can select the best music, the most compatible friends, the most effective beliefs, and the optimal path through life, the question is no longer whether the recommendation is accurate. The question is whether a completely optimized life still preserves the process through which a self is formed.

The human task of the post-AI era may therefore not be to prove that humans remain better than machines at some jobs. That competition places human value in the wrong location from the beginning.

The more important distinction is between activities whose meaning comes from their outcomes and activities whose meaning comes from the fact that a person participates in the process.

Recursive self-improvement may never produce a smooth and unlimited exponential curve. It may encounter diminishing returns, become trapped by a flawed evaluator, slow down at physical experiments, or stop amid institutional conflict. No particular future should be treated as inevitable.

But whenever cognitive production begins to move faster than human understanding and institutional adaptation, a more general problem appears:

When answers are produced faster than humans can understand, verify, and choose among them, how do we remain the authors of our own future?

That may be the real post-AI problem created by recursive self-improvement.

The central question is not whether machines continue becoming more intelligent. It is whether, as intelligence becomes part of the environment, humans preserve the capacity to define direction, demand a pause, understand consequences, and change their minds.

What we need may be more than aligned intelligence. We may need an intelligence willing to leave time for us.

title: 潜空间里的第二层认知
excerpt: 从文字、书籍到互联网，人类一直把记忆与推理的一部分搬到身体之外。下一步也许不是更快地向 AI 输入语言，而是让一个本地模型成为可持续耦合的外置认知层。
html:
真正的下一代界面，也许既不是 GUI，也不是语音，而是 cognition itself。

大多数人把脑机接口想象成一种更快的输入设备：不用手打字，只要在脑中想一句话，电脑就把它写出来。但这仍然沿用了键盘的逻辑——人的思想必须先被压缩成语言，再传给机器。

我更感兴趣的是另一种可能：未来每个人都拥有一个始终在本地运行、长期适应自己的模型。它不只是保存文件或回答问题，而是通过一个低带宽、持续存在的通道，感知人的注意、犹豫、熟悉感、惊讶和方向判断；与此同时，它把检索、模拟、反例和未被注意的可能性送回人的认知回路。模型不再是一项需要主动打开的服务，而更像一层 external cortex——一套位于身体之外、却参与思考过程的认知基础设施。

这听起来很激进，但它并不是突然出现的断裂。它可能只是人类数千年来外置认知的下一步。

一部把心智搬到身体之外的历史

在《斐德若篇》中，苏格拉底借埃及神话批评文字：人一旦依赖外部符号，就会疏于锻炼自身记忆，得到的只是“提醒”而不是“真正的记忆”。Plato, Phaedrus 275a–b

这个担忧并没有错。文字确实改变了人记忆的方式。但它忽略了另一面：文明之所以能够积累，不是因为每个人的大脑装进了更多东西，而是因为经验开始跨越个体寿命，被稳定地保存、复制、校对和重新组合。

可以把这条历史看成一次次认知瓶颈的迁移：

  • 文字把记忆从大脑中的短暂痕迹，变成可以跨时间保存的外部符号；
  • 书籍与印刷把经验从稀缺手稿，变成可复制、可引用、可累积的公共结构；
  • 图书馆与索引把问题从“有没有记录”变成“如何找到记录”；
  • 互联网与搜索引擎进一步外包了寻址。2011 年的实验发现，当人预期信息以后仍可访问时，对内容本身的记忆会下降，却更容易记住去哪里找到它——研究者把互联网描述为一种外部的 transactive memory。Sparrow, Liu & Wegner, 2011
  • 大模型第一次大规模外包的不只是存储和寻址，而是对信息的转换：压缩、解释、比较、改写、生成假设和组织行动。

因此，“外包”不等于“能力消失”。更准确地说，每一种认知技术都会重新安排稀缺性。文字降低了记忆原句的价值，却提高了阅读、判断和重组的价值；搜索降低了记住地址的价值，却让问题定义、来源判断和知识整合变得更重要；大模型降低了生成一个 plausible answer 的成本，于是验证、品味、目标和责任反而成为新的瓶颈。

1945 年，Vannevar Bush 在 As We May Think 中设想 memex：一个按照人的联想路径组织资料的个人知识设备。他甚至在文章结尾追问，是否有一天可以绕过机械输入，直接截取神经系统中的信号。1960 年，J. C. R. Licklider 把目标称为 “Man–Computer Symbiosis”；1962 年，Douglas Engelbart 则把研究对象定义为“人、工具、概念与方法”组成的完整系统，而不是一台孤立的机器。Augmenting Human Intellect

这条路线真正关心的从来不是让机器替代人，而是重新设计“人和工具组成的系统”。

外置记忆之后，是外置认知状态

Clark 和 Chalmers 在 1998 年提出“extended mind”：如果环境中的某个过程，在头脑内部发生时会被毫不犹豫地视为认知过程，那么它在功能上也可以属于认知系统。他们著名的例子是 Otto 的笔记本——它像生物记忆一样稳定、随时可用并指导行动，因此认知系统的边界未必止于皮肤和头骨。The Extended Mind

今天的手机已经接近 Otto 的笔记本，但仍有一个明显断点：大脑与外部工具之间主要靠语言和动作串行通信。

当我读到一个实验结果，最先出现的可能不是一句完整的话，而是一种“这里不太对”的感觉：某个假设与背景知识发生冲突，某个变量似乎被忽略，某个数字带来意外。为了让 AI 帮我继续推理，我必须先完成一连串转换：

  • 把模糊直觉稳定下来；
  • 找到语言表达；
  • 组织成 prompt；
  • 等模型把语言重新编码成内部状态；
  • 再判断它是否理解了真正的问题。

这个过程的瓶颈不一定是打字速度，而是 serialization：一个同时包含多种倾向、置信度和未成形关联的认知状态，被迫压成一条线性的句子。

模型内部也未必必须始终用语言推理。Coconut 等研究尝试让模型把隐藏状态直接作为下一步输入，在连续空间里保留多个可能的推理方向，而不是每一步都过早承诺为一个词序列；目前它仍只是有限任务上的研究原型，而不是“机器已经拥有无语言思想”的证明。Hao et al., Chain of Continuous Thought

但它提示了一个有趣的方向：如果人的某些认知状态和模型的某些计算状态都不必先完整语言化，那么未来界面的目标可能不再是更快地交换句子，而是让两个动态系统共享少量但关键的状态变量。

Latent 不是一门天然存在的共同语言

这里必须做一个重要的纠偏。所谓 brain latent ↔ model latent，不能被理解成大脑和模型内部恰好存在两个可以直接对齐的向量空间。

大脑活动不是一个稳定、统一、可随意读取的 API。它因人而异，会随学习、疲劳、注意和电极漂移发生变化；模型的隐藏状态同样依赖架构、层级、训练目标和版本更新。“latent”只是我们对中间表征的统称，不是一种跨系统通用语。

真正需要被学习的是一个 personal neural adapter：它不负责读取“所有思想”，而是在具体任务中建立可校准的对应关系。

  • 生物侧产生带噪声、个体化、不断漂移的信号；
  • adapter 把信号压缩成少量任务相关的认知变量；
  • 本地模型把这些变量与上下文、长期记忆和当前目标结合；
  • 输出侧先通过屏幕、声音或触觉反馈，未来才可能谨慎探索神经刺激；

所以，这个接口更像两个乐手逐渐学会合奏，而不是翻译器发现了一本早已存在的字典。

第一条有用的通道，可能只有每秒几个 bit

今天的 BCI 已经取得了重要但边界清楚的进展。2023 年，一项侵入式 speech BCI 在一位因 ALS 无法清晰说话的参与者身上实现了每分钟 62 个词的大词表解码，但词错误率仍为 23.8%，研究者明确指出它尚不是完整的临床系统。Willett et al., 2023 2024 年另一项研究在一位参与者身上实现了快速校准和很高的尝试发音解码准确率，说明个体化神经语言接口可以变得更实用，但它仍然是医疗场景中的单参与者结果。Card et al., 2024

非侵入式研究也已经能从 fMRI 中重建受试者听到或想象内容的大致语义，但需要长时间、个体化训练，依赖参与者配合，而且恢复的是语义近似，不是任意、隐秘思想的逐字读取。Tang et al., 2023

这些结果最自然的延伸似乎是追求越来越高的 brain-to-text 带宽。但对认知共生来说，更好的第一个问题也许是：

What is the minimum-bandwidth channel required for useful human–AI cognitive symbiosis?

模型未必需要知道我脑中的完整句子。它也许只需要连续收到几个经过同意、范围受限的信号：

  • 我是否困惑；
  • 当前内容是否出乎预期；
  • 某条路径是熟悉还是陌生；
  • 我对结论的置信度是在上升还是下降；
  • 我想继续、暂停、回退还是拒绝；
  • 我的注意是否遗漏了模型认为重要的分支。

从 Shannon 的通信框架看，接口价值不只取决于原始带宽，也取决于发送的变量是否足以改变接收端的决策。A Mathematical Theory of Communication 对一个已经拥有上下文、个人记忆和世界模型的系统而言，几个 bit 的“方向修正”可能比又一段完整 prompt 更有价值。

这也使近期研究不必等待消费级植入设备。第一代原型可以组合眼动、瞳孔、面部 EMG、键盘节奏、心率和 EEG，在用户明确授权的前提下估计少量认知状态。真正要验证的不是“机器能否读心”，而是：

连续、隐式、低带宽的认知状态通道，能否在不削弱主体性的前提下，提高人机联合推理的质量？

实验可以比较三种条件：普通对话、用户主动报告状态、系统获得受限的隐式状态通道；再测量任务正确率、发现反例的速度、校准度、认知负荷和用户对过程的控制感。最重要的 ablation 不是换一个更大的模型，而是逐个移除 surprise、uncertainty、attention 和 reject 信号，观察哪一类信息真正有用。

为什么它必须 local-first

如果模型处理的只是公开问题，云端服务已经足够方便；如果它持续接触的是注意、犹豫、意向、错误感和神经活动，本地优先就不再只是一个 privacy feature，而是系统边界本身。

本地模型有四个结构性理由：

  • 延迟： 闭环认知反馈必须接近即时，网络抖动会改变人和系统共同适应的节奏；
  • 个体化： neural adapter、个人语义、长期记忆和行为基线高度私人，也高度依赖个人；
  • 连续性： 这个系统需要跨越设备和模型版本保存“我是如何思考的”，而不只是保存聊天记录；
  • 控制权： 用户必须能够断开、检查、回滚和删除认知层，而不是请求远端平台替自己决定。

在设备上运行有用的语言模型已经不是纯粹幻想。Apple 2024 年的技术报告描述了约 30 亿参数的 on-device foundation model；这离持续神经闭环还很远，却说明“个人设备上的模型基础设施”是一条真实的系统路线。Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models

未来的模型可能像电一样成为基础设施：人不再关心每次计算由哪个具体模型完成，就像使用电器时通常不研究电网协议。价值会逐渐从“拥有一个大模型”转移到它上面的认知系统——个人 adapter、长期记忆、可信工具、权限边界、验证机制和与现实世界相连的 agent。

但这个类比也有危险。电改变机器的状态，认知模型可能改变人的信念、注意与目标。因此越是基础设施化，越不能变成不可检查的背景力量。

外置认知层不能成为认知的 rootkit

当反馈从“给你一段文字”变成“改变什么最显眼、什么最熟悉、什么值得继续想”，安全问题就不再只是数据泄露。

谁控制 salience，谁就在影响人的问题空间。谁更新 adapter，谁可能在不改动任何显式记忆的情况下改变一个人的认知习惯。谁拥有长期 cognitive state，谁就拥有比照片、文件和密码更接近人格连续性的资产。

因此，这种系统至少需要五条比今天 AI 产品更严格的原则：

  • 可撤销： 每个输入和反馈通道都能单独关闭，系统断开后人仍能正常行动；
  • 可追溯： 外部建议、个人记忆、模型推断和神经信号必须保留来源边界，不能混成一种“我好像一直知道”的感觉；
  • 最小权限： 一个帮助阅读论文的 adapter 不应顺便推断情绪、政治偏好或健康状态；
  • 本地所有权： 原始神经数据、个体 adapter 和长期 cognitive state 默认不离开设备，云端只接收用户主动选择的最小信息；
  • 认知完整性： 系统不能绕过显式同意去优化人的偏好、注意或行为。

Ienca 和 Andorno 很早就把相关问题概括为 cognitive liberty、mental privacy、mental integrity 和 psychological continuity。Towards New Human Rights in the Age of Neuroscience and Neurotechnology 一旦外置层开始参与前语言阶段的判断，这些不再只是未来伦理学，而会变成操作系统级别的安全需求。

一个可以从今天开始的研究议程

这条路线不应从“训练一个能读出所有思想的模型”开始。更好的研究顺序是：

  • 先找最小通道： 哪几个低维状态最能改善联合推理？需要多少带宽、多少延迟？
  • 再研究共享表征： 如何在特定任务中学习 brain state、behavior signal 和 model state 之间稳定、可解释的 correspondence？
  • 研究共同适应： 人学习如何发出更稳定的信号，模型也适应人的漂移；怎样避免二者一起收敛到脆弱的私有捷径？
  • 建立 epistemic interface： 模型如何把来源、置信度、反例和不确定性送回人，而不是只给一个流畅答案？
  • 解决本地系统问题： 功耗、延迟、持续学习、模型更新、加密存储和设备迁移如何同时成立？
  • 最后才扩大带宽： 只有低带宽闭环证明有价值、可控且可逆之后，才有理由探索更丰富的神经接口。

这里最有生命力的 CS 问题也许不再是“如何训练另一个更大的模型”，而是如何组织一种新的计算原语：intelligence。怎样把它放在用户身边，怎样让它持续学习却不夺走控制权，怎样让人和模型组成的整体比任何一方单独都更可靠。

结尾：从保存经验，到共同生成思考

文字让经验离开了记忆，书籍让经验能够复制，互联网让经验能够被全球寻址，大模型让经验能够被即时重组。每一步都外包了一部分旧能力，同时创造了更高层的新能力和新的依赖。

如果这条路径继续，下一台“个人电脑”也许不再主要是一块屏幕。它保存的核心资产不是 files.zip，而是一个人的模型、记忆、adapter、认知历史和权限边界：一层可迁移、可审计、属于个人的 cognitive state。

那时 AI 确实可能像电一样隐入基础设施。但真正决定未来形态的，不是模型有多大，也不是脑机接口每分钟能输出多少词，而是我们能否建立一种足够紧密、又不吞没人类主体性的耦合。

这才是 human–machine symbiosis 最值得追问的版本：不是机器替我思考，也不是我把思想交给机器，而是让一个由生物脑与外置认知层共同组成的系统，仍然能够知道谁在判断、为什么判断，以及何时应该断开连接。
